_readme: apra-fleet's OWN stray-sweep config, as a fleet-sprint TARGET. The engine owns none of this (docs/generic-engine-boundary.md): it knows no process names, paths or ports of its own. Loaded by packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/sweep-config.mjs and forwarded to every sprint as --sweep-config. See docs/fleet-sprint-getting-started.md section 2.6, whose traps this file is the worked example of. Matching: markers are PLAIN SUBSTRINGS of a process command line with NO path-separator normalization (case-insensitive on Windows only), which is why each path marker is declared in both a POSIX and a Windows form -- a remote Windows member reports 'packages\apra-fleet-se\bin\serve.mjs' and would not match the forward-slash token. WHY THE EVIDENCE CLASSES BELOW ARE WHAT THEY ARE (this is the safety boundary, not cosmetics): a 'path'/'flag' marker makes a process KILLABLE once the engine's other predicates hold, while a 'name' marker can only ever label a candidate and by itself never gets anything killed. The engine's parent-gone predicate is satisfied by ppid 1, so EVERY daemonized fleet process counts as 'parent gone' from the moment its own launcher exits or restarts -- which means productionPorts, below, is the only predicate left protecting a healthy long-lived process that a 'path' marker matches.
_readme_supervisor: fleet-supervisor (bin/serve.mjs) is declared 'path' (killable) because the stale sandbox supervisor left behind on a remote member is the case this sweep exists for. The constraint that makes that safe is a DELIBERATE apra-fleet deployment policy, stated here so it is explicit rather than assumed: on a fleet MEMBER machine the only long-lived apra-fleet listeners are the production fleet MCP server (7523), the production supervisor (8787) and the regression playbook's pair (18700/18701) -- all four enumerated in productionPorts. A supervisor on a member is expected to run on the default port; sandbox supervisors take OS-assigned ports (scripts/sandbox-deploy.mjs) and are throwaway by construction. THE NON-DEFAULT-PORT HOLE IS NOW CLOSED, and is no longer an accepted consequence: a supervisor started with 'serve.mjs --port <other>' and left running still answers HTTP on that port, so the armed liveness probe (livenessProbe below) spares it even though no static productionPorts entry could have named an OS-assigned port. Adding a known long-lived non-default port to productionPorts is still the stronger protection -- it needs no probe tool on the member and protects a process that is hung rather than merely unlisted -- so prefer it where the port is known in advance. WHAT IS STILL KILLABLE, correctly: a supervisor on an unlisted port that answers NOTHING (dead, hung or mid-crash) is exactly the stale process this sweep exists to clear.
_readme_liveness: livenessProbe is set explicitly even though true is the engine default (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/phases/member-prep.mjs, header section 'LIVENESS PROBE: ARMED BY DEFAULT -- DECIDED'), because this file is the worked example other targets copy and a safety predicate should be visible here rather than inherited invisibly. Every candidate that survives all the other predicates gets one HTTP GET per port it holds; anything that answers at all is spared. Fail-safe: a member with no curl / Invoke-WebRequest cannot answer the question, so every candidate there is SPARED and Member Prep prints a loud 'sweep -- LIVENESS UNEVALUABLE' line for that member. On such a member nothing is cleaned up until curl is installed there, or this key is set to false to accept kills that were never checked for life. Set it to false ONLY with that trade understood.
_readme_sprint_engine: fleet-sprint-engine (bin/cli.mjs) is deliberately declared 'name', NOT 'path', so it can never be killed on this evidence. A live sprint child is spawned detached and unref()'d by src/supervisor/spawner.mjs, so its ppid becomes 1 (parent-gone true) the instant its supervisor restarts -- exactly the window src/supervisor/readopt.mjs exists to re-adopt -- and its only listener is an allocateFreePort() viewer port that can never appear in a static productionPorts list. There is no port list that could protect it, so one sprint's Member Prep must not be able to kill another live sprint. Same reasoning for fleet-mcp-server (dist/index.js), which is additionally far too generic a token to ever be treated as evidence.
